qualitative.gate_2_reason: Speculative commodity price-taker lacking pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Reject). Upstream gold mining operator is a speculative commodity price-taker selling an undifferentiated product into global spot markets (LBMA/COMEX) with zero structural pricing power. Gold is neither a non-discretionary Western necessity nor an entrenched, inelastic everyday habit/ritual. Returns on invested capital are entirely cyclical and tethered to volatile bullion spot prices and mining cost inflation.
qualitative.evidence: Newmont is the world's largest gold producer following the 2023 Newcrest acquisition, producing ~6.5M-7M gold ounces annually alongside copper, silver, zinc, and lead. While recent record gold prices ($2,600-$2,900/oz in 2024-2025) drove record free cash flows ($2.9B in 2024, $7.3B in 2025) and a temporary rebound in ROIC (~14% in 2025 from ~8.1% in 2024), its 10-year historical median ROIC sits at a depressed ~6.5%, well below the 12% compounding hurdle. All-in Sustaining Costs (AISC) have escalated significantly due to labor, fuel, and consumable inflation. As a pure commodity price-taker, Newmont has no ability to set prices or earn durable through-cycle excess returns on invested capital independent of bullion market cycles.
